searchText: **c00gan** I’m trying to isolate things people should consider when configuring their validator setup, here’s what I have so far: • Future Proofing hardware for finalization issues and “known unknowns” around Eth1 / Eth2 merge and introduction of sharding (mainly for people who don’t have dynamic plans or not as technically astute to rejigger on the fly (i.e. me)) • To run or not to run an Eth 1 client and instead use Infura endpoint • Virtual vs. local hosting • Eth2 client choice / Slashing protection contingencies What am I missing? Key management. Local/remote signing. ISP plans. Men, tomorrow we ride into battle! Put on your technical and spiritual armour, banish the anxiety and ride into Valhalla! Spears shall be shaken, shields shall be splintered, a sword-day, a red day, ere the sun rises! Ride now, ride now, ride! Ride for ruin and the world's ending! https://tenor.com/view/william-wallace-brave-h-eart-mel-gibson-gif-4951359 Why is this eth2 launch so often associated with violence? https://tenor.com/view/lotr-lord-of-the-rings-horse-charge-gif-17468559 Probably cultural. Any culture with a strong warrior ethos / machismo will be prone to see violence as heroic / epic / awesome. US for example 🙂 Regardless what happens tomorrow my deep respect and congratulations to everyone involved in the design of ETH2.0. Up until a few weeks ago I hadn't read anything about Ethereum and found by chance the Casper paper in the arxiv. In just a few weeks I now understand why people find this design beautiful and challenging it's been addictive. The more you read the more you forget about your own job <@!755590043632140352> A few weeks!?! That's amazing. My address has three transactions: buying 32 ETH, getting some gwei from ethermine (wanted to see how that felt) and sending 32 ETH to the deposit contract 😆 weighing if I'll buy another 32 I should also add to design, my congratulations to those in charge of implementation. Although I believe we're rushing into this without having had a flawless public testnet launch, my interactions mostly with people from prysm but also from guys from Lighthouse, Tekku, Nimbus and Attestant has been an incredible experience. I don't think I've seen this level of dedication 24/7 to support their users in other projects. I hope you get some vacations between genesis and v1.1

excerpts.author: eth2_bridge_bot
excerpts.content:
**c00gan**
I’m trying to isolate things people should consider when configuring their validator setup, here’s what I have so far:

• Future Proofing hardware for finalization issues and “known unknowns” around Eth1 / Eth2 merge and introduction of sharding (mainly for people who don’t have dynamic plans or not as technically astute to rejigger on the fly (i.e. me))
• To run or not to run an Eth 1 client and instead use Infura endpoint
• Virtual vs. local hosting
• Eth2 client choice / Slashing protection contingencies

What am I missing?

excerpts.content: Key management. Local/remote signing. ISP plans.
